# A push rule fired: what to do
1. A key, password or token is listed, or a pushed commit "can no longer be fetched": rotate it first. Revoke it where it was issued, make a new one, update where it lives. Treat it as seen even if the branch is already gone (a PR keeps the commit reachable; only GitHub Support can purge it).
2. Then remove it from the branch: delete the branch, or rewrite its history and force-push the branch (never main). Close any PR; ask GitHub Support to remove cached views for a real secret.
3. A big or design file, no secret: delete or rewrite the branch; put the file in the media home. The six existing tracked files have no exceptions. Files unchanged throughout the scanned range do not enter the scanner's file checks; deletions skip the size/type checks. A later re-save is checked under the ordinary rules. The coordinator's light review 3 supersedes the earlier step-2 exception proposal.
4. A "held" file (git shows it as binary): it was not read, so its contents are unknown, not clean. Look at it before replying `go`; if it may hold a secret, remove it and rotate that secret.
5. "No earlier successful run": expected once, at the first scheduled run after setup. Any later time, find out why (deleted runs, or every run failing) and treat the window as unchecked until a run succeeds.
6. A health alert (a workflow not active, a workflow missing, a PR with no Referee run): George switches it back on (only he changes the walls), and everything since is treated as unchecked. A session tells George what it found (the repo's activity log, the Actions tab); whether any app's or session's access changes is George's decision alone. The cloud apps stay unless he decides otherwise (10/31).
7. A public repo's alert carries no details. The hand-run reads only the repository, its push log and its commits, and posts nothing. A session running as Ace (after the logout; before it, as today) runs it from a clean checkout of main: `GITHUB_REPOSITORY=georgesamuelson/<repo> GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER=georgesamuelson TRUSTED_DIR=. REFEREE_APP_ID=5552272 REPORT_ONLY=1 REPORT_SINCE=<the start time in the run log> bash .github/ci/push-log-scan.sh`. Or, in George's own browser, the repo's Activity page (github.com/georgesamuelson/<repo>/activity) lists every push in the window, and each commit opens there. Neither route needs George's login on the Mac.
8. Close the alert issue with one line on what was done.
Break-glass (only George): if the Referee cannot run (Actions minutes used up, the scanner download fails) and every PR is stuck red, or a governance merge cannot wait for the logout read-back, switch the `main-wall` ruleset to Disabled in the repo's Settings, merge what must merge, then switch it back to Active. The drift check flags a disabled wall until it is restored.
Limits: on a private GitHub Pro repo the push itself cannot be refused; main is guarded only where the Referee's check, bound to the Referee App, is required. Anything holding Actions write can switch off these checks; the outside Watch is the alarm for that. Design: U3 settings bundle r10 (10/31/2026).


## Local setup and activation record

This setup commit does not install a wall or authorize a push, merge, login change, App installation or deployment. `.github/walls.json` is a review record bound to Referee App ID `5552272`, with an unapproved webhook list; it is not the Watch's runtime baseline. The Watch keeps its approved config outside GitHub, and its empty-bypass rule and required push scanners cannot be weakened by that config.

The Apps are created; the public identities recorded by George on 10/31 are:

| Role | Registered App | App ID | GitHub bot login |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| Ace | `ace-samuelson` | 5552138 | `ace-samuelson[bot]` |
| Referee | `referee-samuelson` | 5552272 | `referee-samuelson[bot]` |
| Outside Watch | `watch-samuelson` | 5552292 | `watch-samuelson[bot]` |

Use `ace-samuelson[bot]` wherever a GitHub actor or PR-author login is required. The display author labels from design C remain `Ace (Codex)` / `Ace (Claude)` for the later harness identity setup; these labels are not proof of authentication. This build does not change any local Git author setting.

The Referee workflow supplies the public `REFEREE_APP_ID=5552272` and `ACE_APP_ID=5552138` directly. Both scan workflows also supply `REFEREE_APP_ID=5552272` for App-bound alerts. The outside Watch's existing local config already records `watchAppId: 5552292` and `refereeAppId: 5552272`; its installation ID, freshness window and webhook baseline remain unfinished. No Watch deployment is part of this setup commit.

The source record says the Apps are not installed yet. George supplies `REFEREE_PRIVATE_KEY` and `ACE_PRIVATE_KEY` through the main-only `referee` environment at activation; private key values never belong in source. The Watch key is configured separately at its deployment. No real App keys were read, generated or configured here. Ace's registered grants include Contents/Pull requests write and Actions/Checks/statuses read, with no Workflows access; the Referee requests an Ace token limited to Contents and Pull requests write. The Referee's own token requests only Checks write. It creates its first check before Ace is installed; without a verified wall and installed Ace it cannot publish a successful merge judgment. `MAIN_WALL_VERIFIED=true` follows the actual bound-wall readback. Go counting stays off until the Mac logout and identity proof; only then may `GO_COUNTING_ENABLED=true` be set. `PUSH_LOG_SCAN_INSTALLED_AT` is the reviewed installation time. No local setting was changed by this build.

The Referee reads every changed commit as Git objects using trusted main's scanner and governed list. It never checks out a PR tree. Binary content, symlinks, submodules and case collisions hold. Any failed or incomplete secret scan stays red even after `go`. Removing a `hold` label does not release a PR. A counted `go` is an unedited comment by georgesamuelson with an explicitly null App badge, after the latest recorded server push and the Ace challenge for the exact head and base. An unavailable push record stays held. Every fork PR, and every PR with a null or missing source repository, stays held even when all changed files are routine. Forks cannot count go with the current push-time proof. A source repository that disappears or changes at the final PR refresh also revokes any counted go. After a workflow PR's counted go the check turns green with “George merges this one”; this controller never attempts that merge.

George's 10/31 decision replaces design C's retry cadence with a six-hour backstop (`7 */6 * * *`). A go comment still triggers the Referee at once through `issue_comment`; it does not wait for the backstop. There are 120 scheduled starts per 30 days per repository. At the frozen budget's assumed 1–2 minutes per job plus 5 percent, that adds 126–252 minutes per repository per month. Adding both planned private-repository backstops to phase B changes its estimate from 1,113–2,969 to 1,365–3,473 minutes; ea-jorts alone is 368–760 minutes including its other jobs. These estimates use the existing workload assumptions, not measured runtime; the upper total still exceeds the frozen 3,000-minute allowance assumption. Only ea-jorts' local workflow is changed here. No schedule or account budget was installed by this local build. Merges use Ace and the exact head SHA; GitHub still enforces other required CI.

The separately maintained outside Watch now checks the configured Referee App's completed check runs on each PR head and requests Checks read. Its source is outside this commit; local tests do not prove the actual App grant or live integration. The read-only Watch may not receive bypass_actors from GitHub; omission alarms instead of passing. App grants, the approved webhook inventory, live check binding, badge identity, activity coverage, cloud startup, phone delivery and P1–P9 remain unproven until George's authorized live checks.

Routine files are non-executable `.md` or `.txt` files inside `docs/`, `plans/`, `research/`, `sessions/`, `transcripts/`, `correspondence/` or `reference/`. Executable mode `100755`, hidden root names or path components inside folders, dependency inputs and the existing special-file checks hold; governed paths keep their precedence. Merge commits anywhere in an outstanding PR range are rejected: rebase instead. The shared push scanner also refuses merge-containing ranges. Main is squash-only, so normal PR landings have one parent and scan normally; no main exception is present. Root files, including `GEMINI.md` and other root Markdown, hold unless governed.

Keep the repository setting **Allow auto-merge OFF**. The native disarm mutation is removed. Main allows squash merging only: merge commits and rebase merging stay off. Ace submits its own squash request pinned to the exact head SHA; the desired required-check rule is strict (up-to-date branches). These are local settings records, not proof of installation, and they do not make a green workflow PR mergeable exclusively by George. Referee jobs use separate PR-number concurrency groups; the scheduled whole-repository pass has its own group. Comment jobs run only for original comments by `georgesamuelson` or `ace-samuelson[bot]`.

Every Referee run reads repository metadata. Unless `allow_auto_merge` is explicitly false, every assessed PR gets a failed check saying "auto-merge must stay off" and no merge is attempted. Ace is not requested in that state. Immediately before a merge PUT, the Referee reads the PR again and refuses a changed head or a newly present hold label, even after a previously counted go. An unchanged initial hold with its counted go retains the existing approval path; the read/PUT pair is not an atomic label transaction.

The outside Watch must alert if `allow_auto_merge` ever becomes true. This is recorded as a pending configuration requirement outside the repo; the current Watch has no repository-setting check, so the note is not an implemented or deployed alarm.
